title: Bahrain cracks down on Shiite clerics as Iran attacks
author: Elizabeth Hagedorn
text:
Analysis

Bahrain cracks down on Shiite clerics as Iran attacks

The strikes come as Bahrain targets Shiite clerics accused of ties to Iran, whom human rights groups say are being imprisoned for their beliefs.

Elizabeth Hagedorn

A man walks past a banner depicting Bahrain's (R to L) King Hamad bin Isa al-Khalifa and Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad al-Khalifa in Souq Bab al-Bahrain, in Manama, on Feb. 14, 2026. — Giuseppe CACACE / AFP via Getty Images

You're reading an excerpt from Al-Monitor Washington, where we break down the latest in US-Middle East diplomacy. To read the full newsletter, sign up here.WASHINGTON — Bahrain has imprisoned dozens of Shiite clerics while under Iranian attack, the latest in a crackdown that risks drawing the small Gulf country further into the confrontation between Tehran and Washington.Days after Iran resumed airstrikes on US targets in Bahrain, a Bahraini criminal court on Monday sentenced 64 defendants to life in prison and five others to 15-year terms over alleged collaboration with the Iranian government. The mass trial was marred by allegations of torture, forced confessions and incommunicado detention, according to a joint statement from 20 rights organizations, including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch. Prosecutors said the defendants worked with Iranian officials to bring Bahrain under Iran's influence “by force and unlawful means,” seeking to overthrow the government through "incitement to commit terrorist acts." They were also accused of spreading "wilayat al-faqih," the doctrine of clerical rule at the heart of the Islamic Republic.
